title: A small river: the 50-year flood
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. Thirty years of annual peak flows (m³/s) at a small river. Fit a lognormal distribution.

Give the fitted ln-mean μ and ln-standard deviation σ (four decimals), the 50-year flood (the 0.98 quantile, one decimal), and the annual exceedance probability of 300 m³/s, P(X > 300) (four decimals).

In the Workbench: **Continuous distribution**, **Distribution** *Lognormal*, **Parameters from** *Fitted to a data column*, **Value of interest** 300, **Probability for the quantile** 0.98.

MoreThan.says: That is the non-exceedance probability, P(X ≤ 300). The exceedance probability is the chance a year's peak is larger: 1 minus it.

hints: μ and σ are the mean and standard deviation of ln(peak).
The T-year flood has exceedance probability 1/T: the 50-year flood is the 1 − 1/50 = 0.98 quantile.
